guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / spinal injury and helmet removal
title: Helmet removal after motorcyclist seizure
setting: Motorcycle rally. Rider had a seizure while riding, crashed at low speed. Unresponsive, wearing full-face helmet, gurgling/snoring breathing.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive patient with a compromised airway (gurgling due to helmet/position), wearing a helmet, and high risk of spinal injury. Sick: immediate airway protection.

evolving.narrative: The patient's breathing stops completely as the airway becomes fully occluded by the helmet position.

shared.airway: Compromised, gurgling due to helmet and position

history.history: Had a seizure while riding, lost control and crashed into grass verge 5 minutes ago
history.drugs: Prescribed anticonvulsant medication (forgot to take today)

followUp.question: What is the priority management step for this patient following their seizure?

options.text: Maintain the airway, monitor for further seizures, and place in the recovery position if unresponsive
Restrain the patient to prevent further injury if they start seizing again
Place an object in their mouth to prevent them from biting their tongue
Administer their oral anticonvulsant medication immediately

followUp.explanation: Post-seizure (postictal) patients require careful airway management. If unresponsive, they should be placed in the recovery position (with spinal precautions if trauma is suspected, like removing the helmet safely using two people if the airway is compromised). You should never restrain a seizing patient, put objects in their mouth, or give oral medications to someone with an altered level of consciousness.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999. Stabilize head and spine. Reassure patient, keep warm.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected spinal injury. Maintain neutral alignment. Check BGL, monitor vitals. Airway is compromised and breathing is slow. Safely remove helmet immediately using two-person technique, clear airway, and place in recovery position using log-roll.
